en: Meet them and fight,
And bring turmoil to Beijing!
Strike that swine, Lord Kongurbai,
And crush him like chaff;
Cut off his head, bind it on,
And bring it specially as a gift
To your sworn father, the master smith!
My orphan, son of the keen warrior,
Gird your waist with perfect skill!
Against the Chinese who cover the earth,
Enter alone and attack.
Beijing, where no frail old man can tread—
Disgrace if you let yourself be defeated there.
You wild youth who takes refuge,
Your life is entrusted to God!
Against the Chinese who throng the earth,
You have set out alone on holy war;
Upon the toilsome Black Chinese,
You intend to pursue the blood-price.
May your news come from the campaign,
May your journey lead back from Beijing;
A hero’s work is risk itself—
You are going forth to meet it!
The Kakanchin is the foe you will fight;
God knows whether you will die,
God knows whether you will return—
You are going forth to die!
You have begun the journey to Beijing,
Leaving the many Argyn and Kyrgyz people,
Leaving your camp desolate!
They say Beijing is a distant land,
One no one has seen from afar;
For a traveler who goes without tiring,
They say the road is six months long.
If one circles Great Beijing,
It has a lake that takes long to traverse;
If one goes straight, some roads
Cross a desert forty days wide.
Beijing is no cheap and easy land,
No people of Andizhan
To be taken and left gaping.
My beloved one who gives me comfort,
Go safely and return unharmed;
Come back quickly and do not make us pine!
Hero Bölökbai said these words,
Then all the equipment from the treasury
He gave and entrusted to him;
The infidel spoke in lament,
And every weapon of war
He entrusted to Semetey.
Bölökbai, the master smith,
Was the sheath to his sword;
To my father, gone into eternity,
He truly had been a support at the waist.
The dear hero Bölökbai, master smith,
From the treasury palace
Brought out the equipment.
Among all that equipment,
The finest was Akkelte.
When this gun was slung on,
It was a mirror upon the shoulder;
When one entered battle with the foe,
It was a shield for the entrusted life.
Its straight shooting was proven before the people,
An inheritance remaining
From your father, the bloodthirsty leopard.
Almabash, surpassingly sharp,
Its bullet did not waver at long range;
It made no distinction between far and near.
If you must shoot at the Chinese,
This is the treasure left by your father!
Its lamb-liver-shaped core was set firm;
This was the sharp weapon that never shifted.
When one stared and took aim,
Dust rose from the place aimed at;
Among enemies who heard its voice,
Reason fled and life departed.
From my noble hero’s palace,
Yesterday, when the villains seized it,
A clumsy dog who knew no secret
Had taken my champion’s gun
And treated it as an outcast.
Every one of its riflings was ruined;
The living gun, that wondrous creature,
Had gone into mourning.
Saying, “It will not take fire when I shoot,”
The scoundrels—damn your father’s grave—
Gripped the gun by its muzzle
And smashed it against a stone.
Its stock had broken apart.
Poor Bölökbay,
I repaired its stock again,
So the prince might shoot far,
So his enemy in combat
Might lie utterly ruined.
I twisted it twelve times,
And repaired it to be just like
Butcher King Manas's gun.
So Kongurbay, khan of Beijing,
Might stand and face him,
So he might carefully pull its trigger
And strike the warrior firmly,
So it might wreak havoc
Among the teeming Chinese,
So if my sultan enters battle
He might take the ancient vengeance
Of his royal father Manas,
So when he aims it at the enemy,
Its bullet might roar away,
And tear through the head
Of the enemy who comes against him,
I twisted its barrel ten times.
Brave Manas's Akkelte,
Almambet's Syrbarang,
Khan Bakay's Kökchybyk,
Ajybay's Chortkelte,
Brave Chubak's Koychagyr—
As an unattainable inheritance,
For their far-striking sharpness,
So the sons left behind them
Might choose and take them as gifts,
Grow to manhood from orphanhood,
And bring conflict to Beijing,
Shed blood in close combat,
And from the wrathful warrior,
From infidel Khan Kongurbay,
Fight and exact blood payment,
Live to take revenge,
And through enmity avenge their grievance.
There are twelve sharp, straight guns;
If you wage battle against the khan,
This is what I have prepared for you.
Listen, honored sons!
There will be no regret when you fire them,
If you unleash great conflict upon the khan.
I knew from the beginning
That you would go to teeming China;
I always thought you would go.
How could things be right if you did not?
If you did not go to Beijing,
I thought my departed King Manas
Would be as though buried in salt.
So I kept these prepared.
I prepared twelve identical sharp guns,
So you might fire in encirclement,
And be filled with joy.
Preparing all their powder and shot,
I gathered forty Kalmyks,
Without letting one person notice,
Without letting anyone know,
And had this wonder made.
I had earth dug and saltpeter
Boiled without cease for seven years;
I cast bullets from lead
And had the weapons made ready.
I poured and boxed the powder
And had this wonder fashioned.
For the twelve sharp guns,
I had all the cast bullets
Divided into twelve separate lots.
For all those bullets together,
I had rawhide saddlebags made
And filled them with shot and powder.
Such is the nature of a campaign:
No man goes to teeming Beijing
Without making preparation.
This arduous wonder I have made—
My dear sons, listen!
When you face them, fire,
And go on campaign to Beijing;
Remember me then
As your lame ritual father!”
Thus Bölökbay finished
The warrior's speech.
Treasurer Bölökbay,
Ah, your dear ritual father!
Within the treasury itself,
At the side of the exit door,
Were five guest palaces,
Built exceedingly strong.
To the mouth of that treasury
No man not fated to die went;
Whoever entered without care
Never escaped suffering.
At the treasury entrance stood
Poor Khan Bölökbay's
Champion guards.
With saddlebags full of bullets,
Their knees bending to the ground,
Many champions lifted them.
They ran carrying twelve saddlebags
Of bullets and powder,
And entrusted them
To the prince, the butcher's son.
After Bölökbay gave him these,
Brave Semey, son of Manas,
Your lion who had studied the lesson, said:
“My ritual father Bölökbay,
We should devote ourselves to you!
My falcon father was a khan;
Thinking the inheritance left by my father
Was gone when my father died,
I find there is a man like my father!
I have courage and fierce longing,
And all my equipment is complete.
I may entrust myself to God;
I will set right whoever attacks me!
I will gird my waist firmly,
And overthrow whoever I face.
If fate arrives, I will die.
Kongurbay is lord
Of heavenly Beijing city;
I will wage fierce war
And thus avenge my father
Who departed this world!
I will campaign against the khan;
If Almighty Allah supports me,
I will unleash a calamity
Upon the black-hearted Kalmyks.
Without bringing slaughter and taking captives,
Without spilling blood and taking revenge,
I will not cease while any remain alive,
Nor cease fighting for six months.
Without learning the ground by scouting,
Without raiding horses from Champang,
How could I fail to fight
The warrior like a black mountain,
Whose courage is high and venom strong,
Who sets right whoever attacks him—
The wrathful infidel,
Warrior Khan Kongurbay!
If I do not take revenge, let me die;
If I do not pursue my father's blood price,
Let me sink childless!
Against the Chinese, swollen like a bladder,
I will wage fierce struggle.
If my strength suffices against the infidel,
I will subdue the Gün-zhang-zhung people,
And inflict bitter grief.
I will avenge Almambet,
My beloved ritual father!
The one I will fight is Kakan-Chyn;
The one I lost is brave Chubak;
The one I will war against is Kongurbay.
I have continued the tale from tradition,
And asked those who knew.
The distant road takes six months;
Until I return after six months,
Farewell, my grieving people!
I will travel outward for three months,
And return for three months;
I will come in the sixth month.
If I do not come in the sixth month,
Kakan-Chyn is the one I fight,
And I will have perished and died!
I am going to see
